object_description: single island-like school block enclosing a planted park
design_condition: The school block forms an island around a planted interior park, responding to the site's gravel-pit topography while the cultural center is placed separately and the sports halls are sunk into the ground.

positive.statement: The single building establishes a strong island-like presence in dialogue with the surrounding bars.
The central planted park adapts well to the site's particular topography.
Covered ground-floor openings provide appropriation, transparency, and an intimate school identity.
The central park creates strong social and bioclimatic potential.
The ring distribution creates meeting and transition spaces around the courtyard.
The peripheral classroom arrangement gives the interior distribution clear organization.
The patios provide protected rooms and corridors with natural light.
The project offers coherent water management, permeable surfaces, planting, and green roofs.
The constructive approach and energy operation are effective.

negative.statement: The access to the buried sports halls raises questions about quality and safety.
The horizontal and vertical distribution and entrance spaces remain schematic.
Peripheral classrooms are exposed to noise that would have been better protected centrally.
The proposal needs a more nuanced and less repetitive response.
Outdoor spaces lack complementary atmospheres, appropriations, freshness, and biodiversity.
The audience organization and hall-stage sequence are unclear and do not work.
The documentation center is complicated and unconvincing.
Fully buried sports halls raise concerns about leakage routes, daylight, vandalism, and planting.
Several sports and service spaces have inadequate connections or dimensions.
The foyer and refreshment bar lack a view toward the triple hall.
The circus location in the parking area is inadmissible.
The facade and surroundings contrast unfavorably with the quality of the central park.
Uniform corner openings fail to address their different contexts and functions.
The building's proportions and typology resemble a higher-education building rather than a secondary school.
Noise exposure, typology, and distributions remain unresolved on the upper floors.
The large buried volumes require substantial excavation and mechanical ventilation.
Protection against summer overheating remains insufficiently developed.
